# Bottom line {.unnumbered}

> **EIF4A3 is a credible *differential* dependency — more essential in Y-negative (LOY) than Y-positive (CTRL) HT1080 cells — but it is a "differential essential," not a clean synthetic lethal, and it carries real caveats.**
>
> - All 4 sgRNAs deplete in LOY at the screen endpoint; the effect is **D0-independent** (rests on the direct POST_LOY vs POST_CTRL contrast, not the unreliable 21%-mapping D0 baseline).
> - **MAGeCK-MLE** Wald-FDR = 4.1e-10 and **drugZ** rank 26/19,084 (FDR 0.027) both call it; **MAGeCK-RRA** agrees on direction (LFC −4.47, rank 123) but does not clear FDR (0.59).
> - Decisive test: among **1,206 common-essential genes**, EIF4A3 is the **28th most LOY-skewed (top 2.3%)** — so its signal is *not* explained by generic essentiality.
> - Caveats: it is a common-essential gene (a confounding class), there is a mild genome-wide essential "drift" toward LOY (~−1 log2, hinting at an arm-level proliferation difference), and the data are noisy (effectively 2–3 informative guides).
> - **Confidence:** moderate-to-good that the differential is real; lower that it is a *specific* genetic interaction rather than a sensitized-background effect. Needs isogenic validation.

---

# 1. What EIF4A3 is, and why it's here

EIF4A3 (eIF4A-III) is the **core DEAD-box helicase of the exon junction complex (EJC)**. It is **autosomal** and a **pan-essential** gene (listed in both `CRISPRInferredCommonEssentials.csv` and `AchillesCommonEssentialControls.csv`). Unlike the screen's X–Y paralog candidates, it has **no Y paralog**, so any LOY-specific dependency would be **indirect** — there is no obvious mechanistic anchor.

The screen compares **LOY (Y-) vs CTRL (Y+)** HT1080 cells. The primary, D0-independent comparison is **POST_LOY vs POST_CTRL**; a negative log fold change (LFC) = depletion in LOY = candidate LOY dependency.

```{r essentiality-check}
ess_files <- c(
  AchillesCommonEssential = p("resources/AchillesCommonEssentialControls.csv"),
  CRISPRInferredCommonEssentials = p("resources/CRISPRInferredCommonEssentials.csv")
)
ess_hit <- sapply(ess_files, function(f) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  any(grepl(paste0("^", GENE, "\\b"), x))
})
kt(data.frame(reference_set = names(ess_hit), contains_EIF4A3 = unname(ess_hit)),
   "EIF4A3 is a known common-essential gene")
```

---

# 2. Library coverage and counts

EIF4A3 is targeted by **4 sgRNAs** in the Brunello library. Column order in the count files is
`D0_CTRL · D0_LOY · POST_CTRL_REP1 · POST_CTRL_REP2 · POST_LOY_REP1 · POST_LOY_REP2`.

```{r counts}
raw  <- read.delim(p("count/ht1080_screen2_R1.count.txt"), check.names = FALSE)
norm <- read.delim(p("count/ht1080_screen2_R1.count_normalized.txt"), check.names = FALSE)

raw_g  <- raw[raw$Gene == GENE, ]
norm_g <- norm[norm$Gene == GENE, ]

# short guide ids
short_id <- function(x) sub("EIF4A3_(\\d+)_.*", "g\\1", x)

raw_show <- raw_g
raw_show$sgRNA <- short_id(raw_show$sgRNA)
kt(raw_show, "Raw counts (MAGeCK count output)", digits = 0)
```

```{r counts-norm}
norm_show <- norm_g
norm_show$sgRNA <- short_id(norm_show$sgRNA)
num_cols <- sapply(norm_show, is.numeric)
norm_show[num_cols] <- round(norm_show[num_cols], 1)
kt(norm_show, "Control(NTC)-normalized counts", digits = 1)
```

At the endpoint, every guide collapses in **LOY** while staying high in **CTRL**. The D0 columns are inflated by the broken D0 normalization (21% mapping) and should be ignored.

```{r counts-fig, fig.height=5}
post_cols <- c("POST_CTRL_REP1","POST_CTRL_REP2","POST_LOY_REP1","POST_LOY_REP2")
m <- as.matrix(norm_g[, post_cols]); rownames(m) <- short_id(norm_g$sgRNA)
bar_cols <- c("#377EB8","#377EB8","#E41A1C","#E41A1C")
op <- par(mar = c(5,4,3,1))
bp <- barplot(t(m), beside = TRUE, col = bar_cols, border = NA,
              ylab = "Normalized read count", main = "EIF4A3 sgRNAs: POST timepoint (blue = CTRL, red = LOY)",
              legend.text = post_cols,
              args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8))
par(op)
```

# 3. Statistical results across methods

```{r helper-read}
read_tsv0 <- function(f) read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE)
pick_row  <- function(df, gene, col = 1) df[df[[col]] == gene, , drop = FALSE]
```

## 3.1 MAGeCK-RRA (primary POST_LOY vs CTRL) and time courses

```{r rra}
rra_files <- c(
  `POST_LOY vs POST_CTRL (primary)` = "test/POST_LOY_vs_CTRL.gene_summary.txt",
  `POST_LOY vs D0_LOY (LOY time course*)` = "test/POST_LOY_vs_D0_LOY.gene_summary.txt",
  `POST_CTRL vs D0_CTRL (CTRL time course*)` = "test/POST_CTRL_vs_D0_CTRL.gene_summary.txt",
  `D0_LOY vs D0_CTRL (baseline*)` = "test/D0_LOY_vs_D0_CTRL.gene_summary.txt"
)
rra <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rra_files), function(nm) {
  d <- read_tsv0(p(rra_files[[nm]]))
  r <- pick_row(d, GENE, "id")
  data.frame(comparison = nm,
             neg_lfc   = as.numeric(r$`neg|lfc`),
             neg_pval  = as.numeric(r$`neg|p-value`),
             neg_fdr   = as.numeric(r$`neg|fdr`),
             neg_rank  = as.integer(r$`neg|rank`),
             good_sgrna = as.integer(r$`neg|goodsgrna`))
}))
kt(rra, "MAGeCK-RRA results for EIF4A3. *Time-course/baseline rows depend on the unreliable D0 arm — interpret with caution.", digits = 4)
```

**Read:** the primary POST_LOY-vs-CTRL contrast gives **LFC −4.47, rank 123/19,114, 4/4 good guides**, but **neg|FDR = 0.59** — RRA's permutation FDR is conservative/noisy with only 2-vs-2 replicates. The D0-based rows look dramatic but are not trustworthy for this gene (see §5).

## 3.2 MAGeCK-MLE (LOY treatment effect)

```{r mle}
mle <- read_tsv0(p("results/mageck_mle/ht1080_filtered_norm.gene_summary.txt"))
r <- pick_row(mle, GENE, "Gene")
mle_tab <- data.frame(
  coefficient = "loy_treatment",
  beta = as.numeric(r$`loy_treatment|beta`),
  z = as.numeric(r$`loy_treatment|z`),
  wald_p = as.numeric(r$`loy_treatment|wald-p-value`),
  wald_fdr = as.numeric(r$`loy_treatment|wald-fdr`)
)
kt(mle_tab, "MAGeCK-MLE — strongly significant LOY effect (D0-independent model).")
```

## 3.3 drugZ (synthetic-lethal score)

```{r drugz}
dz <- read_tsv0(p("results/drugZ/LOY_vs_CTRL.txt"))
r <- pick_row(dz, GENE, "GENE")
dz_tab <- data.frame(
  sumZ = as.numeric(r$sumZ), numObs = as.integer(r$numObs),
  normZ = as.numeric(r$normZ), pval_synth = as.numeric(r$pval_synth),
  rank_synth = as.integer(r$rank_synth), fdr_synth = as.numeric(r$fdr_synth)
)
n_genes_dz <- nrow(dz)
kt(dz_tab, sprintf("drugZ — rank %d of %d genes.", dz_tab$rank_synth, n_genes_dz))
```

## 3.4 CRISPRcleanR-corrected (copy-number bias)

```{r ccr}
ccr <- read_tsv0(p("crisprcleanR/results/mageck_corrected.gene_summary.txt"))
r <- pick_row(ccr, GENE, "id")
ccr_tab <- data.frame(num_sgrna = as.integer(r$num),
                      neg_lfc = as.numeric(r$`neg|lfc`),
                      neg_fdr = as.numeric(r$`neg|fdr`))
kt(ccr_tab, "CRISPRcleanR-corrected MAGeCK — CN correction collapsed EIF4A3 to 1 surviving guide; lower-confidence.")
```

## 3.5 Method comparison at a glance

```{r method-summary}
summ <- data.frame(
  Method = c("MAGeCK-RRA (POST_LOY vs CTRL)", "MAGeCK-MLE (loy_treatment)",
             "drugZ (synth)", "CRISPRcleanR + MAGeCK"),
  Effect = c(sprintf("LFC %.2f", rra$neg_lfc[1]),
             sprintf("beta %.2f", mle_tab$beta),
             sprintf("normZ %.2f", dz_tab$normZ),
             sprintf("LFC %.2f", ccr_tab$neg_lfc)),
  Significance = c(sprintf("FDR %.2f", rra$neg_fdr[1]),
                   sprintf("Wald-FDR %.1e", mle_tab$wald_fdr),
                   sprintf("FDR %.3f", dz_tab$fdr_synth),
                   sprintf("FDR %.2f", ccr_tab$neg_fdr)),
  Calls_hit = c("No (direction yes)", "Yes", "Yes", "No"),
  Depends_on_D0 = c("No", "No", "No", "No")
)
kt(summ, "All four methods agree on direction (depletion in LOY); they disagree on whether it clears significance.")
```

# 4. sgRNA-level detail

```{r sgrna}
sg <- read_tsv0(p("test/POST_LOY_vs_CTRL.sgrna_summary.txt"))
sg_g <- sg[sg$Gene == GENE, ]
sg_show <- data.frame(
  guide = short_id(sg_g$sgrna),
  control_mean = round(as.numeric(sg_g$control_mean), 1),
  treat_mean   = round(as.numeric(sg_g$treat_mean), 1),
  LFC = round(as.numeric(sg_g$LFC), 2),
  FDR = signif(as.numeric(sg_g$FDR), 3)
)
sg_show <- sg_show[order(sg_show$LFC), ]
kt(sg_show, "Per-sgRNA stats (POST_LOY vs CTRL). All four guides depleted; g25930 carries the strongest signal, g25931 is low-abundance/uninformative.")
```

---

# 5. Why drugZ's score is "only" normZ −3.96

A natural question: if all guides drop, why isn't drugZ's score more extreme? The answer is mechanical, and mostly an artifact of **very deep sequencing** interacting with drugZ's **fixed pseudocount** and **10M renormalization**.

```{r drugz-mech}
post_raw <- raw[, post_cols]
depth <- colSums(post_raw)
scale_to_10M <- 1e7 / depth
mech <- data.frame(sample = post_cols,
                   total_reads = depth,
                   drugZ_scale = round(scale_to_10M, 4))
kt(mech, "Samples are sequenced extremely deep; drugZ rescales each to 10M reads (a 25-45x shrink).")
```

```{r drugz-cap}
# drugZ-style normalized control abundance + the pseudocount floor on a fully depleted guide
pc <- 5
ctrl_norm <- rowMeans(sweep(as.matrix(raw_g[, c("POST_CTRL_REP1","POST_CTRL_REP2")]), 2,
                            scale_to_10M[c("POST_CTRL_REP1","POST_CTRL_REP2")], "*"))
loy_norm  <- rowMeans(sweep(as.matrix(raw_g[, c("POST_LOY_REP1","POST_LOY_REP2")]), 2,
                            scale_to_10M[c("POST_LOY_REP1","POST_LOY_REP2")], "*"))
cap <- log2(pc / (ctrl_norm + pc))                 # log2FC floor if treatment -> 0
obs_fc <- log2((loy_norm + pc) / (ctrl_norm + pc))  # observed drugZ-style log2FC
capdf <- data.frame(guide = short_id(raw_g$sgRNA),
                    ctrl_norm_reads = round(ctrl_norm, 1),
                    loy_norm_reads = round(loy_norm, 1),
                    log2FC_floor_if_zero = round(cap, 2),
                    observed_log2FC = round(obs_fc, 2))
capdf <- capdf[order(capdf$observed_log2FC), ]
kt(capdf, "After the 10M rescale, EIF4A3's control guides sit at only ~17-41 reads. With pseudocount = 5, even complete dropout caps each guide's log2FC near -2 to -3.2 (g25931 at ~1 read is uninformative).")
```

```{r drugz-genomewide}
# genome-wide SD of per-guide LOY-vs-CTRL log2FC (the z-score denominator scale)
allc <- rowMeans(sweep(as.matrix(raw[, c("POST_CTRL_REP1","POST_CTRL_REP2")]), 2,
                       scale_to_10M[c("POST_CTRL_REP1","POST_CTRL_REP2")], "*"))
alll <- rowMeans(sweep(as.matrix(raw[, c("POST_LOY_REP1","POST_LOY_REP2")]), 2,
                       scale_to_10M[c("POST_LOY_REP1","POST_LOY_REP2")], "*"))
allfc <- log2((alll + pc) / (allc + pc))
gw_sd <- sd(allfc)
cat(sprintf("Genome-wide per-guide LOY-vs-CTRL log2FC: mean = %.3f, SD = %.3f (n = %d guides)\n",
            mean(allfc), gw_sd, length(allfc)))
cat(sprintf("So a guide at log2FC = -3 maps to roughly z = %.1f; drugZ then averages over guides\n", -3/gw_sd))
cat(sprintf("and reports normZ = standardize(sumZ / sqrt(numObs)). For EIF4A3: sumZ = %.2f, normZ = %.2f.\n",
            dz_tab$sumZ, dz_tab$normZ))
```

**Three compounding causes**, ranked:

1. **Depth + fixed pseudocount.** The 25–45× rescale pushes EIF4A3's control guides to ~17–41 reads, where a +5 pseudocount caps complete dropout at only −2 to −3.2 log2 (not the −6 to −8 the raw ratios suggest). *This is the dominant effect and is largely a parameter artifact.*
2. **One dead-weight guide.** g25931 (~1 normalized control read) carries no information but still counts toward the `√numObs` divisor.
3. **Distribution-relative averaging.** normZ divides by `√4` and standardizes against a synthetic-lethal tail already **crowded with common-essential genes** (EIF4A3 among them), so even a clean dropout lands at "merely" rank 26.

The whole chain is self-consistent: normZ −3.96 → one-sided p = 3.8e-5 → BH × 19,084/26 → **FDR 0.027**. Lowering drugZ's pseudocount (e.g. `-p 1`) would un-cap the fully-depleted guides — but it would shift *every* gene, so one must re-rank rather than compare to the current run.

---

# 6. Is it genuine? A critical assessment

The key risk for a **common-essential** gene is that a differential dropout reflects **arm-level differences in proliferation/doublings** (which deplete *all* essentials more in one arm), not a specific genetic interaction. We test this directly, **without using D0**.

## 6.1 No global "LOY depletes everything harder" artifact at the top

```{r essential-balance}
perc <- read.csv(p("results/module8_essential_depletion_per_condition.csv"))
top <- head(perc[order(perc$LFC_CTRL), ], 12)
kt(top[, c("Gene","category","LFC_CTRL","LFC_LOY")],
   "Top-depleting essentials deplete SIMILARLY in both arms (often slightly more in CTRL) - no gross arm-level essential blow-out.", digits = 2)
```

> Note: EIF4A3 is **NA** in this module-8 table because that analysis uses the broken D0 baseline. Hence we switch to the D0-independent POST_LOY-vs-CTRL contrast below.

## 6.2 Decisive test: EIF4A3 vs the common-essential distribution

```{r essential-outlier, fig.height=5}
ess <- readLines(p("resources/AchillesCommonEssentialControls.csv"), warn = FALSE)
ess <- sub("\\s.*$", "", ess)          # take gene symbol before space/paren
ess <- ess[ess != "" & ess != "Gene"]

gs <- read_tsv0(p("test/POST_LOY_vs_CTRL.gene_summary.txt"))
gs_ess <- gs[gs$id %in% ess, ]
lfc_ess <- as.numeric(gs_ess$`neg|lfc`)
names(lfc_ess) <- gs_ess$id

eif_lfc <- lfc_ess[GENE]
rank_in_ess <- sum(lfc_ess < eif_lfc) + 1
pct_in_ess <- 100 * rank_in_ess / length(lfc_ess)

stat <- data.frame(
  metric = c("n essential genes scored", "essential-class median LFC",
             "essential-class mean LFC", "EIF4A3 LFC",
             "EIF4A3 rank among essentials", "EIF4A3 percentile (lower = more depleted)",
             "EIF4A3 LFC minus essential-class median"),
  value = c(length(lfc_ess), round(median(lfc_ess),3), round(mean(lfc_ess),3),
            round(eif_lfc,3), sprintf("%d of %d", rank_in_ess, length(lfc_ess)),
            sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_in_ess), round(eif_lfc - median(lfc_ess),3))
)
kt(stat, "Among common-essential genes, EIF4A3 is a strong outlier for LOY-skewed depletion.")

# histogram
op <- par(mar = c(4.5,4,3,1))
hist(lfc_ess, breaks = 40, col = "grey80", border = "white",
     xlab = "POST_LOY vs CTRL  neg|LFC  (common-essential genes)",
     main = "EIF4A3 sits in the LOY-depleted tail of essential genes")
abline(v = eif_lfc, col = "#E41A1C", lwd = 3)
abline(v = median(lfc_ess), col = "#377EB8", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", bty = "n",
       legend = c(sprintf("EIF4A3 = %.2f (top %.1f%%)", eif_lfc, pct_in_ess),
                  sprintf("essential median = %.2f", median(lfc_ess))),
       col = c("#E41A1C","#377EB8"), lwd = c(3,2), lty = c(1,2))
par(op)
```

**This is the strongest evidence the signal is real:** among genes that are *all* essential, EIF4A3 is one of the ~28 most LOY-skewed (top ~2%). Generic essentiality cannot explain that, and neither can RNA expression (LOY-vs-CTRL RNA logFC ≈ 0.15, FDR 0.71 — not differentially expressed).

## 6.3 The yellow flag: a mild genome-wide essential drift

```{r drift}
drift_mean <- mean(lfc_ess)
cat(sprintf("Essential-class mean LFC (LOY vs CTRL) = %.2f\n", drift_mean))
cat("A non-zero essential-class shift toward LOY suggests a modest arm-level proliferation/doubling\n")
cat("difference. EIF4A3 rides ~", round(abs(eif_lfc - median(lfc_ess)),1),
    "log2 ON TOP of that drift, so it is not merely the drift - but the drift's existence is\n")
cat("exactly the confounder that makes differential-essential hits hard to trust without validation.\n")
```

```{r ledger}
ledger <- data.frame(

    "Most conservative method (RRA) does not clear FDR (0.59)"
  )
)
kt(ledger, "Evidence ledger.")
```

---

# 7. Verdict and next steps

**Verdict:** a **credible differential dependency worth validating — not a confirmed LOY-specific vulnerability.**

- Confidence that the POST differential is **real**: *moderate-to-good* (driven by the top-2% outlier status among essentials, multi-method directional agreement, and D0-independence).
- Confidence that it reflects a **specific genetic interaction** rather than a sensitized-background / proliferation effect: *lower* (it is a common-essential gene with no Y paralog and no mechanistic anchor; a mild arm-level essential drift exists).

**To move it from "interesting" to "genuine":**

1. **Isogenic competition / dropout assay** (the planned `results/isogenicz/` analysis) — the only clean way to separate LOY-specific from background-essential.
2. **Quantify the arm-level drift** — check passage/doubling records; re-rank EIF4A3 against the essential-class distribution (done here: still ~−3.8 after subtracting the median) rather than against all genes.
3. **Understand the module8 NA** — confirm it is only the D0 baseline filter and not a guide-quality problem.
4. Optional: re-run drugZ with a smaller pseudocount and re-rank, to confirm the conclusion is robust to the scoring artifact described in §5.
